findings.title: The guide says the stream's connection is shut down "only once both halves are closed"
findings.claim: The guide says the stream's connection is shut down "only once both halves are closed". The same patch says a few lines earlier that closing the client aborts any open stream, and connection errors also stop the stream connection without either half being closed.

findings.title: The new stream_close() comment says _error is set only by the stop() that follows
findings.claim: The new stream_close() comment says _error is set only by the stop() that follows. That is wrong: abort() also sets _error, and abort() is called from send()'s failure path, from client::abort_all_streams(), and on receive-loop errors.

findings.title: The test comment says the frame 'must be refused', but the test never asserts that…
findings.claim: The test comment says the frame 'must be refused', but the test never asserts that closed_error was thrown. A successful send_empty_frame() is also accepted silently.

findings.title: The test never exercises the second half of the fix, the wait in stream_close() for…
findings.claim: The test never exercises the second half of the fix, the wait in stream_close() for `_outgoing_queue_ready`. Removing that wait would still pass.

findings.title: The test waits with no timeout for the wrapped data_sink::close() to be entered
findings.claim: The test waits with no timeout for the wrapped data_sink::close() to be entered. If stream_close() is not reached (for example, the order of the close halves changes or the stream closes on another path), the test hangs instead of failing.

findings.title: Cleanup in the test is not exception-safe
findings.claim: Cleanup in the test is not exception-safe. An early BOOST_REQUIRE failure, or a send exception other than closed_error, skips release_close.set_value(), sink_closed.get() and server_done.get(). Teardown then either blocks forever on the parked close or hits SEASTAR_ASSERT in ~sink_impl because the sink was never closed.

findings.title: The test assumes the negotiation count and order: exactly 2 hooks, with the stream's…
findings.claim: The test assumes the negotiation count and order: exactly 2 hooks, with the stream's hook last. It also keeps a reference into the growable std::vector of hooks.

findings.title: hook_capturing_compressor_factory mutates itself from a const negotiate() through…
findings.claim: hook_capturing_compressor_factory mutates itself from a const negotiate() through const_cast<...*>(this). The file's existing convention for state changed inside a const negotiate() is a `mutable` member.

findings.title: The test data_sink wrapper hard-codes buffer_size() as 8192 instead of forwarding to the…
findings.claim: The test data_sink wrapper hard-codes buffer_size() as 8192 instead of forwarding to the inner sink, which every other override does. The socket wrapper also replaces set_reuseaddr/get_reuseaddr with a no-op and a constant false.

findings.title: The stream shutdown contract is now written in three places that must stay in sync:…
findings.claim: The stream shutdown contract is now written in three places that must stay in sync: doc/rpc-streaming.md, the sink doxygen, and the source doxygen. The sink doxygen also restates the connection-shutdown rule that belongs to the connection.

findings.title: The new test_data_sink_impl overrides only put(std::span<
findings.claim: The new test_data_sink_impl overrides only put(std::span<...>), and without a SEASTAR_API_LEVEL guard. That pure virtual exists only at API level 9 and above, and the build still lets you pick level 7.

findings.title: The test holds `auto&` to `client_factory
findings.claim: The test holds `auto&` to `client_factory.hooks.back()`, a reference into a std::vector that negotiate() keeps growing with push_back.

findings.title: The new comment says nothing else waits for `_outgoing_queue_ready` and that…
findings.claim: The new comment says nothing else waits for `_outgoing_queue_ready` and that stop_send_loop() waits for `_sink_closed_future`. In fact stop_send_loop() still moves `_outgoing_queue_ready` into when_all() together with `_sink_closed_future`.

findings.title: `_stream_closing` is a second "no more sends" flag that only connection::send() checks
findings.claim: `_stream_closing` is a second "no more sends" flag that only connection::send() checks. Other send-gating code still checks only `_error` or sink_closed(): the error() accessor, sink_impl send_buffer/close, and client::enqueue_zero_frame, which is documented as an "enlightened copy" of send().

findings.title: The public compressor contract for send_empty_frame() isn't updated, although the hook…
findings.claim: The public compressor contract for send_empty_frame() isn't updated, although the hook can now fail with closed_error on a live, not-yet-errored stream connection.

findings.title: The new docs say dropping an unclosed sink "is an error"
findings.claim: The new docs say dropping an unclosed sink "is an error". In fact ~sink_impl() hits SEASTAR_ASSERT(sink_closed()), a fatal process abort.

findings.title: The docs tell you to 'drain what is still in flight' to release a source, but don't say…
findings.claim: The docs tell you to 'drain what is still in flight' to release a source, but don't say that this wait is unbounded unless the peer closes its sink.

findings.title: hook_capturing_compressor_factory duplicates the existing send_empty_frame-capturing…
findings.claim: hook_capturing_compressor_factory duplicates the existing send_empty_frame-capturing tracker::factory/compressor fixture a few lines above (lz4_fragmented delegate, the same empty-data compress idiom, and the same abort() legacy negotiate) instead of reusing it.

findings.title: The test's data_sink wrapper hard-codes buffer_size() to 8192 and does not forward it to…
findings.claim: The test's data_sink wrapper hard-codes buffer_size() to 8192 and does not forward it to the inner sink, as it does for every other method, which changes the stream connection's output_stream buffering compared with production.

findings.title: Judgment call: the test waits on close_entered_cv with no timeout, and relies on a magic…
findings.claim: Judgment call: the test waits on close_entered_cv with no timeout, and relies on a magic 10 yields to 'let the batch flush poller run'.

findings.title: Judgment call: the root-cause narrative is repeated nearly word for word in the test's…
findings.claim: Judgment call: the root-cause narrative is repeated nearly word for word in the test's header comment, the rpc.cc comments, the rpc.hh field comment and the commit message.

findings.title: Only the client-side stream connection, and only the close_sink() route into…
findings.claim: Only the client-side stream connection, and only the close_sink() route into stream_close(), are tested. The server-side stream connection's hook and the close_source()-triggered stream_close() are not.

findings.title: The new docs say a source is closed by reading it until it 'throws'
findings.claim: The new docs say a source is closed by reading it until it 'throws'. That is wrong when the throw comes from deserialization: unmarshall exceptions propagate without close_source() being called, so the source stays open.

findings.title: Commit f545c28a changes behavior without its regression test
findings.claim: Commit f545c28a changes behavior without its regression test. The test arrives separately in 5e25ebdb, so the fix commit is not self-proving.

findings.title: stream_close() now waits for the previous _outgoing_queue_ready before closing the write…
findings.claim: stream_close() now waits for the previous _outgoing_queue_ready before closing the write buffer, with no timeout or cancellation. Each queued entry's own send timeout or cancel only withdraws non-front entries, and the front entry can block indefinitely on a peer that stops reading. sink::close() therefore inherits an unbounded wait before eof is even attempted, and neither the commit message nor the PR body mentions this latency or cancellation effect.

findings.title: test_connected_socket_impl is a thin pass-through that copies the entire…
findings.claim: test_connected_socket_impl is a thin pass-through that copies the entire net::connected_socket_impl interface (about 15 overrides) only to wrap sink(). The file already has loopback_socket.hh/rpc_socket_impl infrastructure with an error-injection hook point.

findings.title: The new test types have vague names (test_sink_state, test_data_sink_impl,…
findings.claim: The new test types have vague names (test_sink_state, test_data_sink_impl, test_socket_impl) that hide their specific role. They park data_sink::close() until released and record puts that arrive after close.

findings.title: stream_close() moves _outgoing_queue_ready out and leaves a ready future in its place,…
findings.claim: stream_close() moves _outgoing_queue_ready out and leaves a ready future in its place, so stop_send_loop()'s when_all(_outgoing_queue_ready, _sink_closed_future) no longer tracks the queue directly. Its unchanged comment still says _outgoing_queue_ready might be exceptional because of queue drain, which no longer holds for stream connections.

findings.title: The test's closing comment claims that without the fix ~output_stream() asserts at that…
findings.claim: The test's closing comment claims that without the fix ~output_stream() asserts at that point. The test's only assertion is put_after_close, and the empty-frame refusal is accepted silently whichever way it goes (try/catch with no requirement). So the test does not prove the refusal itself, and the 10-yield loop is an arbitrary bound for the flush poller.
